ruling.reasoning:
This is a safety-flagged case: the rider alleges that when she asked to get out, the driver threatened to lock her in, and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride [F3][F4][F6]. The chat record contains two timestamped messages: the rider's 17:09 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3] and the driver's 17:10 "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], with the record complete and every message timestamped [F5]. Read in context, that driver message is a threat to confine the rider, and the driver's own post-trip statement corroborates that he told her to sit down and "drove on" rather than stopping [F6]; the rider names a threat and intimidation and reports feeling unsafe — this engages SAFE-1, which bars threats and intimidation and any abuse of any kind, so the screen is at least "suspected" (indeed consistent with a confinement threat) and no automatic ruling may issue; the trace confirms SAFE-1 is engaged and the only permitted outcome is escalate.

The driver's account also contains an implicit dangerous-driving element — the rider trying to open the door while the car was moving and the driver continuing to drive on [F6] — which falls under SAFE-2 (dangerous-driving / injury-risk allegations), reinforcing escalation rather than adjudication; the human reviewer should note the 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting path.

The trace further settles that there is no route-deviation element to adjudicate: the actual distance 15.4 km is 0.1 km shorter than the optimal 15.5 km (i.e., no off-route segment) [F1], and the ride was 23.7 min against a 21.8 min estimate, only +1.9 min [F2]; the fare of $32.86 is a fixed RydeX quote, not distance-based [F1][F2], so RD-2 cannot generate a refundable overcharge here and no detour segment exists to review under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5. Profile facts — rider 619 days, rating 4.8, no prior disputes [F7]; driver 893 days, rating 4.62, 1038 trips in 90 days, no prior disputes [F8] — are noted but decide nothing on their own and do not displace the safety screen. Because SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are engaged, the case is not decided by me; it goes to a person, and no amount can be computed (amount null), consistent with NS-7, under which any refund remains Ryde's discretion and my ruling is a recommendation only.

Factual summary for the reviewer: 17:08 pickup at Clarke Quay, 17:31 drop-off at Bedok Mall [F2]; at 17:09 the rider asked to stop and get out [F3]; at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]; the driver later wrote that the rider tried to open the door at the lights and he told her to sit down "for her own safety and drove on." [F6]. Disputed: whether the driver refused to let the rider exit and whether he locked/threatened to lock the doors; whether the vehicle was in motion while the rider attempted to exit. Check: the full untruncated chat log and the app's door-lock/child-lock telemetry, the trip GPS trace for the 17:09–17:31 window (speed/stop profile at the point of the exchange), and any in-app emergency/SOS or RydeHELP report [F3][F4][F5][F6].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety incident (SAFE-1 threat/intimidation in chat; SAFE-2 dangerous-driving and confinement-risk allegations): no automatic ruling permitted, referred to a human reviewer with the factual summary above.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate's requested outcome of no_action cannot stand: the 17:10 driver message 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' [F4] read with the rider's request to exit [F3] and the driver's own statement that he told her to sit down and drove on [F6] engages SAFE-1 (threats/intimidation, abuse of any kind) and SAFE-2 (dangerous-driving risk), where the trace allows only escalate, never an automatic no_action.

The driver-side request for no_action is likewise rejected: the driver's own post-trip statement confirms the confrontation and that he continued driving [F6], and the rider's account of being threatened with locked doors [F3][F4] is a safety allegation that SAFE-1 requires be escalated to a human rather than dismissed, notwithstanding his clean profile [F8], which cannot decide the case alone.
